summary: Full backend+frontend test of forgot-password/reset-password flow. Backend: 8/8 pytest tests pass (fixture-domain forgot returns 200 and writes password_resets doc; wrong code=400 'Invalid or expired verification code'; expired code=400; short password=400; no doc=400; happy-path reset+relogin works; login lockout is cleared on reset; unknown email returns 200 to prevent enumeration). Frontend: /auth forgot-password-link switches to 'Reset your password' heading with forgot-info text; submitting fixture email qa.reset.<rand>@example.com produces toast 'Check your inbox — your 6-digit verification code is on its way (valid for 10 minutes).' and transitions to 'Enter your code' screen with reset-code-input + new-password-input visible. Fixture domain @example.com correctly skipped by provider (email_utils.FIXTURE_EMAIL_RE).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py forgot_password: on 502/503 from send_email the password_resets doc is deleted (good) but the outer response still returns the generic 'ok:true' text only when no exception — the raise path returns 503/502 correctly. Behavior matches spec.
email_utils.send_email retries up to 3 times on 429 with 2s/4s backoff; consider capping total wait or making it configurable so a single forgot request doesn't block a request thread ~6s.
reset_password uses constant-time-ish sha256 hash compare via != — acceptable since code_hash is sha256 hex; still, hmac.compare_digest would be defense-in-depth.
seed_data_creation: Multiple pwreset_*@example.com and qa.reset.*@example.com fixture users created via /api/auth/register (session-end conftest purges @example.com).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Forgot/reset flow verified end-to-end. Backend test file is /app/backend/tests/test_password_reset.py (8 tests, all passing). Fixture-domain regex in email_utils prevents provider calls to @example.com/@x.com/@example.org.
